authors: Ahmadzadeh R, Bergeron L, Tang M et al.
title: The superior and inferior gluteal artery perforator flaps
note: About 5 superior and 8 inferior gluteal perforators of at least 0.5 mm on each side, along two lines across the buttock.

authors: Alexandrou ME, Gkaliagkousi Ε, Loutradis C et al.
title: Haemodialysis and peritoneal dialysis patients have severely impaired post-occlusive skin forearm vasodilatory response assessed with laser speckle contrast imaging
note: Reactive hyperaemia in forearm skin by laser speckle imaging: after an occlusion, flow rises 187% above baseline and peaks about 11 s after release.

authors: Álvarez-Prats D, Carvajal-Fernández O, Valera Garrido F et al.
title: Acupuncture Points and Perforating Cutaneous Vessels Identified Using Infrared Thermography: A Cross-Sectional Pilot Study
note: Infrared thermography finds perforating cutaneous vessels at acupuncture points.

authors: Benias PC, Wells RG, Sackey-Aboagye B et al.
title: Structure and Distribution of an Unrecognized Interstitium in Human Tissues
note: Fluid-filled spaces supported by collagen bundles in submucosae, dermis, fasciae and perivascular tissue — a body-wide interstitium.

authors: Bohlen HG
title: Arteriolar closure mediated by hyperresponsiveness to norepinephrine in hypertensive rats
note: Arterioles held closed by nerves: cutting them opened 22% more third-order arterioles in normal rats.

authors: Bolton B, Carmichael EA, Stürup G
title: Vaso-constriction following deep inspiration
note: The inspiratory gasp reflex: a deep breath constricts the skin’s vessels within seconds.

authors: Burton AC
title: On the physical equilibrium of small blood vessels
note: Why a small vessel can snap shut: with active tension in its wall, Laplace's law leaves it no stable open state below a critical pressure.

authors: Cagnie B, Barbe T, De Ridder E et al.
title: The influence of dry needling of the trapezius muscle on muscle blood flow and oxygenation
note: A single dry-needling stimulus raises local blood flow and oxygenation in the trapezius for fifteen minutes.

authors: Charkoudian N
title: Skin blood flow in adult human thermoregulation: how it works, when it does not, and why
note: Skin blood flow is set by sympathetic nerves and local temperature: from minimal levels under local cooling to 6–8 L/min in heat.

authors: Chen Q, Bensamoun S, Basford JR et al.
title: Identification and quantification of myofascial taut bands with magnetic resonance elastography
note: Taut bands identified and quantified with magnetic resonance elastography.

authors: Clifford PS, Kluess HA, Hamann JJ et al.
title: Mechanical compression elicits vasodilatation in rat skeletal muscle feed arteries
note: Muscle feed arteries squeezed shut widen within seconds of release: by 16% after one 1 s compression, 14% after one of 5 s, and 27% after five of 1 s. Repeated compressions add up; a longer one does not.

authors: Cutting C, Ballantyne D, Shaw W et al.
title: Critical closing pressure, local perfusion pressure, and the failing skin flap
note: Skin flaps show the critical closing phenomenon: blood does not flow until perfusion pressure passes a threshold set in part by vascular smooth muscle tone.

authors: de Dear RJ, Arens E, Hui Z et al.
title: Convective and radiative heat transfer coefficients for individual human body segments
note: How fast skin loses heat: about 4.5 W/m²·K by radiation and 3.4 W/m²·K by convection in still air.

authors: Dorsher PT
title: Myofascial referred-pain data provide physiologic evidence of acupuncture meridians
note: Trigger-point referred-pain patterns track the acupuncture meridians.

authors: El Assar M, García-Rojo E, Sevilleja-Ortiz A et al.
title: Functional Role of STIM-1 and Orai1 in Human Microvascular Aging
note: Human small arteries from donors over 65 contract more strongly to adrenergic stimulation; force is close to maximal at 90% of the circumference they would have at 100 mmHg.

authors: Farias M, Maraldi E, Wallenkampf KC et al.
title: Adverse events in meditation practices and meditation-based therapies: a systematic review
note: Across 83 studies, adverse events in about 8% of those who meditated — anxiety and depression most often, suicidal behaviour among them — sometimes in people with no previous mental-health problems.

authors: Fede C, Angelini A, Stern R et al.
title: Quantification of hyaluronan in human fasciae: variations with function and anatomical site
note: Hyaluronan measured in human fasciae: 6 µg/g over trapezius and deltoid, about 30–35 µg/g in fascia lata and rectus sheath, 90 µg/g in the retinacula.

authors: Fede C, Petrelli L, Pirri C et al.
title: Innervation of human superficial fascia
note: The superficial fascia is richly innervated; about a third of its fibres are autonomic, concentrated around vessels.

authors: Fredberg JJ, Jones KA, Nathan M et al.
title: Friction in airway smooth muscle: mechanism, latch, and implications in asthma
note: Airway smooth muscle stretched as in breathing: the latch is a low-friction contractile state, which may be why a deep breath fails to reopen the airways in asthma.

authors: Fredberg JJ, Inouye DS, Mijailovich SM et al.
title: Perturbed equilibrium of myosin binding in airway smooth muscle and its implications in bronchospasm
venue: Am J Respir Crit Care Med 159:959-67
note: The breath keeps airway smooth muscle from freezing: tidal stretch perturbs myosin binding and biases the muscle toward lengthening; without it the muscle virtually freezes at its static length.

authors: Fronek K, Zweifach BW
title: Microvascular pressure distribution in skeletal muscle and the effect of vasodilation
note: Microvascular pressures measured directly: in arterioles of 70 µm and wider, pressure tracks systemic arterial pressure.

authors: Gerwin RD, Dommerholt J, Shah JP
title: An expansion of Simons' integrated hypothesis of trigger point formation
note: The integrated hypothesis of trigger-point formation, expanded.

authors: Gilliatt RW, Guttmann L, Whitteridge D
title: Inspiratory vaso-constriction in patients after spinal injuries
note: The inspiratory vasoconstriction reflex studied after spinal injury — the pathway runs through the sympathetic outflow.

authors: Goto M, VanBavel E, Giezeman MJ et al.
title: Vasodilatory effect of pulsatile pressure on coronary resistance vessels
note: In toned coronary arterioles, a larger pressure pulse at the same mean pressure widens the lumen: the pulse itself dilates, with or without the endothelium.

authors: Hack GD, Koritzer RT, Robinson WL et al.
title: Anatomic relation between the rectus capitis posterior minor muscle and the dura mater
note: The myodural bridge: a band of tissue from rectus capitis posterior minor to the dura at the base of the skull.

authors: Hai CM, Murphy RA
title: Cross-bridge phosphorylation and regulation of latch state in smooth muscle
note: The latch-bridge model: dephosphorylated cross-bridges that hold smooth-muscle tension cheaply.

authors: Heine H
title: Anatomical structure of acupoints
note: About 80% of classical acupoints coincide with perforations of the superficial fascia by a vessel–nerve bundle.

authors: Hong CZ, Simons DG
title: Pathophysiologic and electrophysiologic mechanisms of myofascial trigger points
note: Pathophysiological and electrophysiological mechanisms of trigger points; satellites and key points.

authors: Hubbard DR, Berkoff GM
title: Myofascial trigger points show spontaneous needle EMG activity
note: Spontaneous needle-EMG activity at the trigger-point nidus.

authors: Johansson H, Sojka P
title: Pathophysiological mechanisms involved in genesis and spread of muscular tension in occupational muscle pain and in chronic musculoskeletal pain syndromes: a hypothesis
note: A proposed loop: metabolites of static contraction drive the gamma system and the muscle spindles, raising stiffness and metabolites again, so muscle tension perpetuates itself and spreads to other muscles.

authors: Kelly S, Beardsley C
title: Specific and cross-over effects of foam rolling on ankle dorsiflexion range of motion
note: Foam rolling the calf of one leg increased ankle range of motion in that leg for at least 20 minutes, and in the other, untouched leg for up to 10 — a cross-over effect, perhaps through greater stretch tolerance.

authors: Konrad A, Nakamura M, Warneke K et al.
title: The contralateral effects of foam rolling on range of motion and muscle performance
note: A scoping review: one bout of foam rolling on one limb increases range of motion in the other, untreated limb, most likely through reduced perception of pain. A single bout leaves the other side’s maximal strength unchanged.

authors: Krause WE, Bellomo EG, Colby RH
title: Rheology of sodium hyaluronate under physiological conditions
note: Hyaluronan in physiological saline stays a Newtonian liquid over a wide range of shear rates, with no sign of gel formation without protein.

authors: Langevin HM, Yandow JA
title: Relationship of acupuncture points and meridians to connective tissue planes
note: Eighty percent of acupuncture points, and half the meridian intersections, lie on connective-tissue planes.

authors: Langevin HM
title: Connective tissue: a body-wide signaling network?
note: Connective tissue as a body-wide signalling network.

authors: Langevin HM, Fox JR, Koptiuch C et al.
title: Reduced thoracolumbar fascia shear strain in human chronic low back pain
note: About 20% less shear glide between thoracolumbar fascia layers in chronic low back pain.

authors: Lau YT, Liu CF, Tsai CC
title: Cutaneous vasoconstrictor response induced by inspiratory gasp in relation to sex and age
note: A deep inspiratory gasp cuts fingertip skin blood flow by 59–71%, graded with the depth of the breath.

authors: Lindahl JR, Fisher NE, Cooper DJ et al.
title: The varieties of contemplative experience: A mixed-methods study of meditation-related challenges in Western Buddhists
note: The largest study of meditation-related challenges: pressure or tension that builds and releases, energy, currents, involuntary movement.

authors: Ljung B, Sivertsson R
title: Vibration-induced inhibition of vascular smooth muscle contraction
note: Rhythmic stretch of vascular smooth muscle cuts its active force at once, by an amount set by the stretch's size and rate; even the pulse may ease arterial tone.

authors: Lorenzo S, Minson CT
title: Human cutaneous reactive hyperaemia: role of BKCa channels and sensory nerves
note: The skin's reactive hyperaemia is carried largely by sensory nerves and BKCa channels, not prostanoids.

authors: Macgregor J, Graf von Schweinitz D
title: Needle electromyographic activity of myofascial trigger points and control sites in equine cleidobrachialis muscle--an observational study
note: Horses have trigger points too: the same spontaneous electrical activity found in humans and rabbits.

authors: Maurer N, Nissel H, Egerbacher M et al.
title: Anatomical Evidence of Acupuncture Meridians in the Human Extracellular Matrix: Results from a Macroscopic and Microscopic Interdisciplinary Multicentre Study on Human Corpses
note: Dissection of meridians: tracks in the extracellular matrix, but vessel–nerve bundles at only a few points.

authors: Mayrovitz HN
title: Physiological Impacts and Medical Applications of the Inspiratory Gasp Vascular Reflex
note: The inspiratory gasp reflex reviewed: skin vessels constrict 3.6–3.8 s after a gasp, most deeply at 4.6–5.2 s, and recover over about half a minute.

authors: McNulty WH, Gevirtz RN, Hubbard DR et al.
title: Needle electromyographic evaluation of trigger point response to a psychological stressor
note: Mental arithmetic turned up the electrical activity at a trigger point but not at an adjacent control site — the writer has the address.

authors: Melzack R, Stillwell DM, Fox EJ
title: Trigger points and acupuncture points for pain: correlations and implications
note: The first systematic comparison: a 71% correspondence between trigger points and acupuncture points for pain.

authors: Meng S, Tang Z, Zhu M et al.
title: Perforating cutaneous vessels: A key feature of acupoints - Anatomical evidence from five-Shu acupoints in the upper limbs
note: Dissection of the five-shu points of the arm: perforating cutaneous vessels are a key feature of acupoints.

authors: Miller A, Rola P, Spiegel R et al.
title: Arteriolar Collapse and Haemodynamic Incoherence in Shock: Rethinking Critical Closing Pressure
note: Critical closing pressure read as a binary threshold: arterioles snap shut when smooth-muscle tension exceeds intraluminal pressure, and reopen only when tone falls, external pressure is relieved or inflow pressure rises.

authors: Moraska AF, Hickner RC, Kohrt WM et al.
title: Changes in blood flow and cellular metabolism at a myofascial trigger point with trigger point release (ischemic compression): a proof-of-principle pilot study
note: Microdialysis inside an active trigger point: ischaemic compression brings a transient rise in local blood flow.

authors: Morris SF, Tang M, Almutari K et al.
title: The anatomic basis of perforator flaps
note: A modern synthesis of perforator anatomy region by region.

authors: Mulvany MJ, Warshaw DM
title: The active tension-length curve of vascular smooth muscle related to its cellular components
note: Small arteries' active tension falls with shortening along a line that reaches zero at 0.38 of the optimal circumference: a nearly shut vessel's muscle pulls weakly.

authors: Mulvany MJ, Aalkjaer C
title: Structure and function of small arteries
note: Small arteries, below about 500 µm, actively regulate peripheral resistance: the size class of most perforators.

authors: Murphy RA, Rembold CM
title: The latch-bridge hypothesis of smooth muscle contraction
note: The latch-bridge hypothesis reviewed: in sustained contractions calcium, phosphorylation and ATP use fall while force is held.

authors: Nakayama Y, Shirai Y, Yoshihara K et al.
title: Evaluation of glycosaminoglycans levels in normal joint fluid of the knee
note: Normal knee joint fluid in healthy young adults holds 3.4 mg/ml of hyaluronan: tens to hundreds of times the fascia's.

authors: Neutel CHG, Weyns AS, Leloup A et al.
title: Increasing pulse pressure ex vivo, mimicking acute physical exercise, induces smooth muscle cell-mediated de-stiffening of murine aortic segments
note: Aortic smooth muscle de-stiffens after bouts of high cyclic stretch and re-stiffens slowly; the muscle has to be contracted and stretched for it to happen.

authors: Nichol J, Girling F, Jerrard W et al.
title: Fundamental instability of the small blood vessels and critical closing pressures in vascular beds
note: The companion measurements: whole vascular beds stop flowing at a critical closing pressure, the instability Burton predicted.

authors: Nicholls M, Manjoo A, Shaw P et al.
title: A Comparison Between Rheological Properties of Intra-articular Hyaluronic Acid Preparations and Reported Human Synovial Fluid
note: Healthy synovial fluid, far richer in hyaluronan than fascia, has a zero-shear viscosity of 1–175 Pa·s: an upper bound for any hyaluronan collar.

authors: Quintner JL, Cohen ML
title: Referred pain of peripheral nerve origin: an alternative to the "myofascial pain" construct
note: The alternative: tender points as referred pain of peripheral nerve origin.

authors: Quintner JL, Bove GM, Cohen ML
title: A critical evaluation of the trigger point phenomenon
note: A sceptical review of the trigger-point construct and its circularity.

authors: Rembold CM
title: Relaxation, [Ca2+]i, and the latch-bridge hypothesis in swine arterial smooth muscle
note: In arterial smooth muscle, relaxation is paced by the fall of calcium, not by latch-bridge detachment: the latch holds only while the calcium signal lasts.

authors: Rivner MH
title: The neurophysiology of myofascial pain syndrome
note: Review of trigger-point neurophysiology, including the rabbit work in which the alpha-blocker phentolamine reduces spontaneous activity.

authors: Saint-Cyr M, Wong C, Schaverien M et al.
title: The perforasome theory: vascular anatomy and clinical implications
note: Each perforator supplies its own territory — a perforasome — linked to its neighbours by direct and indirect vessels.

authors: Schiffrin EL, Deng LY, Larochelle P
title: Progressive improvement in the structure of resistance arteries of hypertensive patients after 2 years of treatment with an angiotensin I-converting enzyme inhibitor. Comparison with effects of a beta-blocker
note: Human subcutaneous resistance arteries: the media is 5.2% of the lumen diameter in normotensive people, 7.5-8% in untreated hypertension.

authors: Schleip R, Naylor IL, Ursu D et al.
title: Passive muscle stiffness may be influenced by active contractility of intramuscular connective tissue
note: Fascia can contract on its own, via myofibroblasts.

authors: Segal SS, Duling BR
title: Flow control among microvessels coordinated by intercellular conduction
note: A dilation started at one point on an arteriole propagates along its wall, upstream, independently of flow.

authors: Shah JP, Phillips TM, Danoff JV et al.
title: An in vivo microanalytical technique for measuring the local biochemical milieu of human skeletal muscle
note: The acidic, mediator-rich milieu of active trigger points, sampled by microdialysis.

authors: Shah JP, Thaker N, Heimur J et al.
title: Myofascial Trigger Points Then and Now: A Historical and Scientific Perspective
note: Trigger points then and now: a history from 19th-century “nodules” to microdialysis.

authors: Sikdar S, Shah JP, Gebreab T et al.
title: Novel applications of ultrasound technology to visualize and characterize myofascial trigger points and surrounding soft tissue
note: Trigger points imaged: discrete hypoechoic nodules, stiffer than surroundings, with abnormal flow.

authors: Stecco C, Stern R, Porzionato A et al.
title: Hyaluronan within fascia in the etiology of myofascial pain
note: Hyaluronan-rich loose tissue between fascial layers, and its densification as a substrate of myofascial pain.

authors: Stecco A, Meneghini A, Stern R et al.
title: Ultrasonography in myofascial neck pain: randomized clinical trial for diagnosis and follow-up
note: The loose-connective-tissue sublayers of neck fascia are thicker in chronic neck pain and thin with treatment.

authors: Tang M, Mao Y, Almutairi K et al.
title: Three-dimensional analysis of perforators of the posterior leg
note: Thirteen perforators of at least 0.5 mm in the back of each leg, each supplying about 38 cm²; lower down, septocutaneous perforators arranged lengthwise in one or two parallel chains.

authors: Taylor GI, Palmer JH
title: The vascular territories (angiosomes) of the body: experimental study and clinical applications
note: The arterial road map of the body: ~40 source-artery territories and an average of 374 major perforators per subject. “Arteries follow closely the connective tissue framework of the body.”

authors: Taylor GI, Minabe T
title: The angiosomes of the mammals and other vertebrates
note: Across mammals and in humans, the size and density of the cutaneous perforators follow the skin’s mobility: large and sparse where it is mobile, smaller and more densely grouped where it is tethered or fixed.

authors: Taylor GI, Corlett RJ, Dhar SC et al.
title: The anatomical (angiosome) and clinical territories of cutaneous perforating arteries: development of the concept and designing safe flaps
note: The anatomical territory of one cutaneous perforator, bounded by the anastomoses that link it to its neighbours.

authors: Tesarz J, Hoheisel U, Wiedenhöfer B et al.
title: Sensory innervation of the thoracolumbar fascia in rats and humans
note: The thoracolumbar fascia is densely innervated, including nociceptors.

authors: TRAVELL J, RINZLER SH
title: The myofascial genesis of pain
note: The first maps of myofascial referred-pain patterns.

authors: Trepat X, Deng L, An SS et al.
title: Universal physical responses to stretch in the living cell
note: After a transient stretch the living cell's cytoskeleton fluidizes, in the same way across cell types: a universal physical response.

authors: Whetzel TP, Mathes SJ
title: Arterial anatomy of the face: an analysis of vascular territories and perforating cutaneous vessels
note: Small, densely populated perforators supply the front of the face and the scalp; large, sparse ones in predictable places supply the sides of the face.

authors: Willard FH, Vleeming A, Schuenke MD et al.
title: The thoracolumbar fascia: anatomy, function and clinical considerations
note: The thoracolumbar fascia: anatomy, function and clinical considerations.

authors: Wolfe F, Smythe HA, Yunus MB et al.
title: The American College of Rheumatology 1990 Criteria for the Classification of Fibromyalgia. Report of the Multicenter Criteria Committee
note: The eighteen tender points of the 1990 fibromyalgia criteria.

authors: Woolf CJ
title: Central sensitization: implications for the diagnosis and treatment of pain
note: Central sensitisation: the central amplifier of chronic pain.

authors: Yoshinaga T, Koga T, Koga H
title: Effectiveness of Ultrasound-Guided Hydrodissection for Atypical Anterior Cutaneous Nerve Entrapment Syndrome Presenting as Lower Back Pain Due to Retrograde Neuropathic Pain
note: The whole model in one case: a tender point, a pulsating perforating artery beneath it on Doppler, resolution with hydrodissection.

authors: Zhang RZ, Gashev AA, Zawieja DC et al.
title: Length-tension relationships of small arteries, veins, and lymphatics from the rat mesenteric microcirculation
venue: Am J Physiol Heart Circ Physiol 292:H1943-52
note: Small arteries of about 240 µm develop a maximal active wall tension of 3.4 mN/mm: the strength with which a vessel can close itself.
